title: Wavefront Autoscaler and Tenant Quarantine Playbook
body:
Purpose
This doc captures an end-to-end proposal for a new autoscaling surface were calling "Wavefront Autoscaler" plus an operational pattern called "tenant quarantine". The goal is to give Dedicated customers elastic capacity that (a) preserves latency SLOs for high-fidelity lanes, (b) minimizes unit cost for tail workloads, and (c) contains noisy tenants without cascading impact.

Motivation / Why now
- We see recurring incidents where sudden tenant traffic causes warm-pool starvation and latency regressions on high-priority lanes.
- Existing soft-decommit and credit-pool ideas reduce costs but are brittle when tenants have highly bursty, unpredictable patterns.
- Customers want predictable cost envelopes but also to be able to survive unexpected peaks without full manual intervention.

Design principles
- Latency-first: autoscaler must protect latency budgets for lanes/tenants that have committed SLAs.
- Auditability: every capacity decision must be traceable (trigger, metrics, model, policy).
- Fast containment: isolate misbehaving tenants within seconds-to-minutes without full pool eviction.
- Graceful fallback: when resources constrained, downgrade non-critical work to cheaper fidelity variants rather than dropping requests.
- Operational simplicity: runbook and recovery must be compact and automatable.

High-level components
1) Wavefront Autoscaler (WA)
   - Continuous multi-horizon predictor: short (15s-5m), medium (5m-1h), and daily (1d) horizons. Funnels signals into a probabilistic forecast for per-tenant demand.
   - Headroom fabric: maintains a small elastic warm pool distributed across nodes and racks; WA decides size and distribution.
   - Fidelity aware scaling: WA can scale lanes at different fidelity tiers (full FP32/quantized/trimmed model variants) based on priority and latency risk.
   - Preemptive handshake: WA emits prewarm intents to the serving runtime with a soft-commit and expiry timestamp to avoid over-committing.

2) Tenant Quarantine Layer (TQL)
   - Fast containment channel: when a tenant exceeds anomaly thresholds (error rate, RPS spike, token-per-request surge, KV growth), TQL enforces a progressive policy: gentle throttles -> route to degraded fidelity -> isolate to a soft-sandbox slice -> quarantine (temporary rate-limited sandbox).
   - Quarantine wallet: per-tenant temporary capacity token that decays; tenants can consume it for short bursts but are delayed if they exhaust the wallet.
   - Observability hooks: automatic incident creation (Slack + ticket) with telemetry snapshot for SRE/SE to triage.

Autoscaler algorithm (rough sketch)
- Input signals: per-tenant RPS, tokens/s, latency P50/P95, KV cache hit ratio, warm-count, recent scale events, scheduled business events (from customer metadata).
- Forecasting engine: ensemble of exponential smoothing and short-window LSTM-lite for unusual spikes. Output is a 90th percentile forecast and an uncertainty band.
- Decision rules: if forecasted 90p > current capacity * safety_factor => prewarm N nodes; safety_factor varies by lane priority (e.g., 1.3 for high, 1.7 for low).
- Spread policy: distribute prewarm across availability islands to reduce blast radius.
- Cooldown & decay: warm pool gracefully decays over a configurable window (default 20m) unless forecast reaffirms demand.

Burst economics and quotas
- Quarantine wallet model: each tenant has a baseline monthly burst budget derived from their commit and historic peak patterns. Small transient bursts draw down wallet; when wallet < threshold, additional burst ops are limited or rerouted.
- Cost transparency: tenant-visible page showing burst spend and wallet balance (for Dedicated customers to self-serve).

Isolation controls and precedence
- Priority tiers: committed (SLA-backed), dedup/high-fidelity, best-effort. Policies define preemption order and allowed degradations.
- Fallback matrix: map from current lane to acceptable degraded lane/model variant + expected latency/cost delta.
- Soft-sandbox slices: ephemeral allocation that can run lower-fidelity requests from quarantined tenants with strict rate limits and IO caps.

API & Config surface (product-facing)
- New fields on Dedicated reservation config:
  - autoscale.mode: {off, conservative, wavefront} (string)
  - autoscale.wallet_monthly: integer tokens (customer-facing burst budget)
  - autoscale.priority_override: list of tenant IDs with forced priority
  - isolation.quarantine_thresholds: stringified rule refs (backend interprets)
- Admin endpoints: /ops/wavefront/forecast, /ops/quarantine/status, /ops/wallet/adjust (authenticated ops).

SLO & observability
- New metrics to surface: forecast_90p_gap, warm_pool_coverage, quarantine_entries, wallet_consumed_percent, lane_degradation_rate.
- Dashboards: per-reservation heatmap (latency vs wallet balance), chain of custody for prewarm events (who/what/why).
- Alerts: warn when quarantine_entries > X/min or when wallet_consumed_percent > 80% for > 10m.

Operational runbook (initial)
1) Detection: WA flags a predicted >40% gap for a high-priority lane or TQL triggers anomaly.
2) Automated response: prewarm and apply progressive throttles; if tenant crosses quarantine threshold, move to soft-sandbox slice and notify SRE.
3) Manual triage: SRE checks snapshot (top N tenant requests, model variant, KV growth) and either: increase wallet (ops), approve temporary dedicated hotslot, or coordinate customer fix.
4) Recovery: scale down warm pool on sustained low demand, reconcile wallet usage for billing. Record postmortem if contamination > 30s latency spike.

Safety & abuse mitigation
- Rate-limited wallet top-ups: ops-only and audited.
- Anti-spoofing: tenant metadata signed; also detect cross-tenant traffic patterns.
- Billing guardrails: when a tenant enters quarantine repeatedly in a billing cycle, trigger account review and automated recommendations (model quantization, prefix caching).

Prototype plan & milestones (quarter view)
- Week 0-3: prototype WA predictor and a minimal warm-pool control loop in staging.
- Week 4-7: implement TQL fast-path (throttles + degraded routing) and instrumentation.
- Week 8-12: end-to-end test with synthetic tenant workloads + chaos tests (rack failures).
- Week 13-16: limited alpha on 3 customers (opt-in) + billing exposure toggles.
- Post-alpha: iterate on policies, add wallet UI and ops endpoints.

Risks and unknowns
- Forecasting under long-tailed events: spikes tied to external events (e.g., viral content) may still overshoot, causing cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Customer UX: exposing wallet mechanics might confuse some customers; we need clear defaults and recommendations.
- Edge cases: multi-tenant KV cache pressure can create sudden cross-tenant latency coupling that is hard to isolate without finer runtime hooks.

Open questions (for sync)
- Should wallet be replenished deterministically monthly or decay at a rate?
- How aggressive should preemptive warms be when uncertainty band is large?
- What is the acceptable guardrail for ops to top-up wallet (automation vs manual)?

Next steps / Action items
- @Benji: spin up a small prototype of the predictor (deadline: 2024-11-26).
- @Marta: draft the TQL thresholds and translate them to telemetry queries + alert rules (2024-11-22).
- @Evan: design the soft-sandbox resource limits and implement runtime hooks (2024-12-05).
- Product sync: schedule deep-dive with Sales Eng / Solutions on alpha customer selection (target: 2024-11-29).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic: the WA design favors easier operational traceability over chasing perfect forecasting. Aim is to reduce user-visible incidents and provide predictable billing exposure.
- Please add concrete threshold suggestions in the comments (examples: quarantine on 5x median RPS sustained for 60s, or token-per-request > 3x baseline).

Scratchpad / rough math
- Example: a tenant with baseline 100 rps and burst to 1000 rps for 120s consumes ~ (900 rps * 120s * token_cost) -> roughly how many wallet tokens? Need modeling with actual token-per-request distributions.
- Warm pool sizing rough: keep enough prewarmed slots for top 5% concurrent spike size across tenants; initial conservative default = 10% of pool capacity.

References / links embedded in body:
- forecasting proto ticket: https://linear.app/RD/issue/WF-129-wavefront-autoscaler-proto
- runtime hooks PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842
- ops contract: confluence:Dedicated-telemetry-contracts

End of draft.

(Inline TODOs and thresholds intentionally left fuzzy; want engineering and SRE to propose concrete numeric defaults in next iteration.)
